title: Qualcomm CEO tells Vietnam's president: we want Hanoi as our third-largest AI R&D hub
subtitle: Cristiano Amon met General Secretary To Lam on August 28 and said Qualcomm plans to expand the Hanoi R&D center into the company's third-largest AI research site worldwide.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon met Communist Party General Secretary and President To Lam in Hanoi on August 28. Vietnamese state media reported that Amon told the president Qualcomm wants to develop its Vietnam presence into the company's third-largest artificial-intelligence R&D hub globally. Qualcomm already runs a Hanoi center and has collaborated with Viettel and VinSmart on device-side AI work. Lam separately urged Samsung, in a parallel meeting, to deepen its Vietnam AI and chip investment. The Vietnamese government has framed both engagements as part of a shift toward a growth model built on semiconductors, digital transformation, and AI.

The specific 'third-largest' framing is the news. Qualcomm's top two AI R&D concentrations are San Diego and Hyderabad; putting Hanoi third would place Vietnam ahead of the company's existing sites in Cambridge (UK), Shanghai, Boulder, and Cork. That is a meaningful reshuffling of where mobile-AI silicon and on-device model work happens, and it lands in the same window that Nvidia, Samsung, and SK Hynix have all made publicized Vietnam expansions.

The pattern to watch is broader than one company. Vietnam is positioning itself as the neutral-ground alternative in the U.S.-China semiconductor split — close enough to Chinese supply chains to work at scale, aligned enough with U.S. export controls to attract Western AI investment. If Qualcomm, Samsung, and Nvidia all follow through with substantial Hanoi footprints, on-device AI research and mobile-inference silicon designed there will shape the next generation of consumer AI features globally.

Takeaway for learners: 'where does the R&D happen' is a legitimate proxy for 'who ends up defining the standards.' If you are early-career in AI hardware, mobile ML, or on-device model optimization, Southeast Asia is now a viable location for that work rather than a peripheral one. And if you are watching AI-supply-chain risk, note that the U.S. is no longer the single default center of gravity.
